query: Why do some agents have longer resolution times?

per_column.name: assigned_agent
per_column.rationale: The query is about per-agent resolution times, so an agent identifier is the natural grouping axis. However, the original table already contains 'assigned_to' and 'closed_by', making this column largely redundant. Groundedness is moderate: the sample source texts shown contain no agent name, yet specific agents are confidently produced; presumably these come from the original 'assigned_to' field rather than the shown short_description, but as displayed the values are not clearly supported.

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorising incidents by type gives a genuine axis to explain resolution-time variation (some categories take longer), and is not a bare restatement despite an existing 'category' column since it is derived from the free-text description. The values are well-grounded readings of short_description (database access, VPN, network, software).

per_column.name: issue_complexity
per_column.rationale: Complexity is directly relevant to why resolution times differ, a strong new modelling axis. But groundedness is weak: the short descriptions are terse and give little basis for a low/medium/high complexity judgement. Labels like 'low_complexity' for 'Unable to access the database' appear to be unwarranted confident inferences rather than sound readings of the text.

per_column.name: incident_severity_proxy
per_column.rationale: A severity/impact proxy is a useful lens for explaining longer resolutions. However, assigning 'high_impact_infrastructure' vs 'medium_individual_access' from a one-line description is an inferential leap the source only weakly supports; the specific severity tier is largely asserted, not grounded.

per_column.name: resolution_mechanism
per_column.rationale: The mechanism required to resolve an incident plausibly drives resolution time, so this is analytically valuable. But the source text describes symptoms, not fixes; the table has no resolution notes. Producing 'server_restart_required' for 'Unable to access the database' invents an unstated fact, so values are poorly grounded.

judge.rationale: Most added columns supply genuine new axes (category, complexity, severity, resolution mechanism) directly relevant to explaining resolution-time variation, so table-level usefulness is high; assigned_agent is the weakest due to redundancy with existing 'assigned_to'. Groundedness is the main concern: incident_category reads well from the descriptions, but complexity, severity, and especially resolution_mechanism are confident inferences the terse source text does not clearly support, and no resolution/effort notes appear in the sampled rows to justify them.
